english.title: Attempt breach of a non-molestation order
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without reasonable excuse attempted to do an act, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ACT..), which you were prohibited from doing by a non-molestation order made under section 42 of the Family Law Act 1996
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) of the Criminal Attempts Act 1981.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See also section 42A(2) re liability only when aware of the existence of an order.
(ii) See section 42A(3) re conduct not being punishable as a contempt of court.
(iii) See section 42A(4) re conduct which has been punished as a contempt of court.
(iv) This offence was Inserted into the Family Law Act 1996 by section 1 of the Domestic Violence, Crime and Victims Act 2004.

other.penalty:
Either way -
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and /or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: 5 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2002; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 42A(5)(b) of the Family Law Act 1996 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit on prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
